decisive_items: new onset of fever and worsening chest pain that was retrosternal and sharp in quality
pericardial friction rub located over the left sternal border
diffuse ST-segment elevation on II, III, aVF, and V3-V5 accompanied by PR-segment depression in I and II and PR-segment elevation in aVR
response.rationale: Post-intervention fever, sharp retrosternal pain, friction rub, and diffuse ST elevation with PR shifts indicate acute pericarditis, overriding initial MI findings.

rejected.why: Only captures initial MI features, ignores subsequent pericardial syndrome.
Broad ACS label, less specific than pericarditis for evolving clinical picture.
